 MISSOURI (KOAM) -- The Missouri Cold Weather Rule took effect on Sunday and will continue through March.
 The Cold Weather Rule means that disconnection of heat-related services is prohibited when temperatures are predicted to drop below 32 degrees between 6 a.m. and 9 p.m. for the following 72-hour period.
 In 2025, Senate Bill 4 expanded the forecast protection period from 24 hours to 72 hours, according to the Missouri Public Service Commission.
 If faced with a heat-related utility bill that cannot be paid in full, it is important for customers to:
 Contact the utility company.
 State an inability to pay the bill in full.
 Provide any required eligibility and verification documentation.
 Make a minimum payment if required.
 Enter into a payment agreement if deemed eligible.
 The Missouri Public Safety Commission says additional consumer protections for eligible customers include lenient payment terms, extended payment plans, and additional notification requirements prior to disconnection.
